author: Farodin11
quote:
The graphics and physics are genuinely impressive, and interacting with the world feels surprisingly natural. Whether you are experimenting with the environment, causing chaos, or simply messing around, the sandbox systems are the game’s biggest strength and make it easy to lose hours without a specific objective.
Unfortunately, that is where most of my enthusiasm ends. The game suffers from noticeable technical issues, including bugs and glitches that can undermine otherwise enjoyable moments. The 30 FPS cap is particularly hard to accept in 2026, especially for a game that puts so much emphasis on physics, visual detail, and dynamic interactions. It makes the experience feel less smooth and less polished than it should be.
The characters are also fairly bland, and the story never gave me much reason to care. It feels generic rather than memorable, and the game does not live up to its hype. More importantly, the older games in the series were much funnier because they did not care about political correctness and were willing to mock, offend, and mess with absolutely everyone and everything. This entry feels noticeably safer and more restrained by comparison, which drains much of the irreverent personality that made the earlier games stand out.
Verdict: This is a fun sandbox game, but that is about all it is. If you mainly want a physics playground and impressive world interaction, it can be enjoyable. If you were expecting the sharp, unapologetic humour, memorable characters, and stronger story of the older games, you will be disappointed.
